data.title: Gbeľany – a Púchov culture hillfort later used by the Slavs
data.excerpt: The hillfort above Gbeľany, at 652 m above sea level, belongs among the settlements built by the people of the Púchov culture at the end of the 1st century BC, and it was apparently used again by the Slavs of the pre-Great Moravian period. Not a single written record of it survives, yet pottery and a coin of Matthias Corvinus from 1464 show that the ridge served once more in the 15th century, probably to the armies of the Brethren.

children.text: The Gbeľany hillfort belongs among the settlements built by the people of the Púchov culture at the end of the 1st century BC, and it was later apparently used by the Slavs of the pre-Great Moravian period as well, whose occupation follows on from the preceding periods. Great Moravian sherds were found in 1963 on the fields at the western edge of the village.

The hillfort lies about 2 km to the NE of the village, at a height of 652 m above sea level. The ridge of the hillfort runs from north to south and has two main summits – plateaux in the shape of an irregular oval. The length in the N–S direction is 60 m, in the E–W direction only 30 metres. The total area is 0.16 ha. The path leads up the castle hill along its southern and eastern slopes. The entrance to the hillfort was built on the south-eastern side. At the edge of the hilltop plateau it is possible to trace the ground plan of a former rampart or wall.

The second part of the castle is situated on the northern tip, 75 m to the north, and has the shape of a smaller trapezium. Its dimensions are 24 m in the east–west direction and 14 metres in the north–south direction. This part of the hillfort is visibly enclosed by ramparts and a ditch, and originally probably by a palisade fortification as well. Since the ramparts and the ditch are well preserved, it can be judged that this is the later part of the hillfort. No structural remains can be recognised on the surface.

children.text: There was no written record of the hillfort. Some researchers date the construction of the castle, probably a timber one, to the 12th – 13th century. In an earlier period pottery finds from the Middle Ages were made here. In the Middle Ages, in 1433, the hillfort was occupied together with the height by Strečno castle by the Brethren (bratríci), an army. Dr Moravčík states of this that it was used again only at the beginning of the second half of the 15th century (besides pottery, also the find of a coin of Matthias Corvinus from 1464), probably by the armies of the Brethren, who operated here in the course of the struggles for the Hungarian throne. Under the impact of their failures in the fighting against the army of King Matthias Corvinus, and especially after the defeat at Veľké Kostoľany in 1467, they withdrew to the safer and better-protected sites of northern and north-western Slovakia, where they were still moving about around 1474.
